system:
You are coding NSW motor accident decisions for a research dataset. Read the decision text supplied and assign each ordinal score from the text alone.

Score each dimension INDEPENDENTLY. A decision describing a severe case will score high on some dimensions and not others: severe physical injury does not by itself imply a contested proceeding, a disputed liability, or a prominent psychological component. Judge each scale against its own definition and resist letting an overall impression of severity carry across the scales.

If the text does not support a judgement on a dimension, give the lowest score rather than guessing upward, and say so in `uncertain`.

DECISION TEXT:
--- Catchwords ---
MOTOR ACCIDENTS -

Motor Accident Injuries Act 2017 ; settlement approval; claimant was driving his motor vehicle through an intersection when his vehicle was impacted by the driver of the insured motor vehicle; the claimant sustained soft tissue injuries to the cervical spine, right shoulder and left shoulder, and also was certified by the medical service as suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder and persistent depressive disorder; working reduced hours on light duties; insurer admitted liability; no entitlement to non-economic loss; claim for past and future economic loss plus loss of superannuation; total amount proposed after deduction of workers compensation pay back is $230,176.05 less payback to Centrelink which has yet to be ascertained; Held – proposed settlement is just, fair and reasonable; proposed settlement is approved under section 6.23 (2)(b).

--- Key Paragraphs ---
[para 30] Sets the statutory test under s 6.23 MAI Act for approving settlements.
30. Section 6.23 (2) (3) of the MAI Act requires approval of the settlement, and I am not to approve the settlement unless I am satisfied it complies with any of the requirements of the MAI Act or the Guidelines.

[para 31] Details cl 7.38 Motor Accident Guidelines criteria the Member must be satisfied of.
31. Clause 7.38 of the Guidelines states I must be satisfied as to the following:

(a) the proposed settlement is just, fair, and reasonable and within the range of likely potential damages assessments for the claim were the matter to be assessed by a, taking into the account the nature and extent of the claim and taking into account any proposed reductions or deductions in the proposed settlement, and

(b) the claimant understands the nature and effect of proposed settlement and was willing to accept the proposed settlement.

Preliminary conference on 3 February 2026

[para 33] Finds specific approved heads and net settlement amount; dispositive reasoning.
33. I am satisfied it is appropriate in this matter to assess damages for past economic loss and past superannuation in the sum of $239,126. Tax paid on statutory benefits is $32,000. Damages for future economic loss in the sum of $166,075.38. The net amount of settlement monies payable to the claimant is $230,176.05 less payback to Centrelink which is yet to be ascertained.

[para 14] Sets out the gross settlement sum and deductions; central quantum terms.
14. Accordingly, the insurer has proposed to resolve the matter for an amount of $405,201.38 less payback to the workers compensation insurer in the sum of $175,025.33 and furthermore, less payback to Centrelink, which both parties acknowledge has yet to be ascertained.

[para 15] Breaks down past economic loss components including super and Fox v Wood.
15. The amount proposed for past economic loss is $239,126, which is calculated as follows:

a full loss of earning capacity of $1200 net per week to 16 January 2023, which is the sum of $48,000 (40 weeks multiplied by $1,200);

a 75% loss of earning capacity to 30 December 2025, which is the sum of $138,600 (154 weeks multiplied by $1,200 x 75%);

in addition, the settlement includes loss of past superannuation at rate of 11% which is the sum of $20,526, and

Fox v Wood payment of $32,000.

[para 16] Explains future economic loss method, vicissitudes, and superannuation.
16. In relation to future economic loss, the insurer proposed the following:

$900 per week to age 70.

the amount allowed for future economic loss is calculated as a loss of $900 net per week to age 70 less 15% for vicissitudes which is the sum of $145,044, and

future loss of superannuation at a rate of 14.5% is the sum of $21,031.38. The amount allowed for future economic loss is $166,075.38.

[para 4] Records the insurer’s admission of liability and non-threshold injury acceptance.
4. The insurer wholly admitted liability on 22 May 2024, and after receipt of the Certificate of Medical Assessor Michael Hong, dated 16 February 2024, conceded the claimant sustained a non-threshold injury.

[para 25] Concludes the settlement is just, fair and reasonable within the assessment range.
25. I am satisfied the proposed settlement is just, fair and reasonable and within the range of likely potential damages assessment if the claim was to proceed to assessment, considering the nature and extent of the claim.

Assign each score:
  Injury Burden Intensity (0-4): overall physical burden of the injuries: 0 minimal, 4 catastrophic/multiple major injuries
  Treatment Burden (0-3): extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care: 0 none or minimal, 3 extensive surgery and long-term care
  Work Impact Severity (0-3): loss of working capacity: 0 none, 3 total incapacity
  Legal Procedural Complexity (0-3): procedural complexity of the proceeding: 0 straightforward, 3 heavily contested
  Psychological Injury Emphasis (0-2): weight the decision gives to psychological injury: 0 none, 2 central
  Liability Clarity (0-2): how clear fault is: 0 seriously disputed, 2 clear or admitted
  Causation Complexity (0-2): difficulty attributing the condition to the accident: 0 straightforward, 2 heavily contested
  Pre-existing Condition Salience (0-2): how prominent a prior condition is in the decision: 0 absent, 2 central
